title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: What a Late-Invoice Waiver Is Measured On
content:
## Principle

A late-invoice waiver on Demurrage and Detention Free Time demurrage releases charges that the line was entitled to bill but can no longer collect, because it was invoiced after the deadline. An overcharge — any part of the line's invoiced figure above what the line comes to when it is priced again from the recorded movement dates and the product on the record — was never such a charge, and no part of an overcharge is ever contained in a late-invoice waiver.

## The amount still open

The open amount of the late demurrage line is read from the account. It is the line's billed amount after subtracting whatever waivers, the operations department's included, and dispute credits have so far been booked with the line as their reference; nothing else is subtracted, and the figure never drops below nothing.

## Entries and the open amount (hypothetical figures, line invoiced at 1000.00)

| Entry on the account | Booked with the late line as its reference? | Open amount |
|---|---|---|
| none | not applicable | 1000.00 |
| operations-department waiver of 100.00 | yes | 900.00 |
| dispute credit of 60.00 | yes | 940.00 |
| card payment of 200.00 on the record | no, a payment names no invoice line | 1000.00 |
